judge_input.description:
### Description

This PR implements `mockThrow(foo)` and `mockThrowOnce(foo)`, doing so as shorthands for `mockImplementation(() => { throw foo })` and for `mockImplementationOnce(() => { throw foo })` respectively.

Having a non-error path plus an error path for the synchronous functions (that is, `mockReturnValue` together with `mockThrow`) is something that mirrors the asynchronous counterparts (namely `mockResolvedValue` together with `mockRejectedValue`), and it goes on to make the synchronous error paths immediately visible and intention-revealing right there in the tests.

I'm perfectly open to renaming these two if that is something that happens to be wanted, though. I did go and consider `mockThrownValue`, but in the end I just didn't really end up seeing the need for it.

> [!NOTE]
> `pnpm run test` → All pass  
> `pnpm run test:ci` → Fails due to an existing test that is skipped only when `GITHUB_ACTIONS` is set
>
> Affected test: `test/cli/test/watch/stdin.test.ts:93`  
> As far as I'm aware, it's unrelated to the changes here in this PR.

### Please don't delete this checklist! Before submitting the PR, please make sure you do the following:
- [ ] It's really quite useful if your PR happens to reference an issue somewhere, one where it is discussed ahead of time in advance. If the feature is a substantial one, or if it goes and introduces breaking changes of some kind without any discussion first, then the PR might well end up being closed on you.
- [X] Ideally, what you should go and do is to include a test, specifically one that fails without this PR being in place but then goes on to pass once it actually is.
- [X] Please, do not go and make any changes at all to the `pnpm-lock.yaml` file, unless it happens to be the case that you are also introducing a brand new test example along with it.
- [X] Please go ahead and check the [Allow edits by maintainers](https://docs.github.com/en/pull-requests/collaborating-with-pull-requests/working-with-forks/allowing-changes-to-a-pull-request-branch-created-from-a-fork) option, so as to help make the whole review process go faster than it would. Do note that this particular option is not one that is available for any of the repositories that happen to be owned by Github organizations.

### Tests
- [X] Go ahead and run the whole set of tests, doing so by way of the `pnpm test:ci` command.

### Documentation
- [X] If you happen to introduce any new functionality, then do go ahead and document it (you are able to run the documentation with the `pnpm run docs` command).

### Changesets
- [X] The changes over in the changelog are the ones generated automatically from the PR name. Please, do make very sure that it explains your changes in a manner that is understandable, and please do prefix each of the changeset messages with `feat:`, `fix:`, `perf:`, `docs:`, or else `chore:`.

+## mockThrow <Version>4.1.0</Version> {#mockthrow}
+
+```ts
+function mockThrow(value: unknown): Mock<T>
+```
+
+Accepts a value that will be thrown whenever the mock function is called.
+
+```ts
+const myMockFn = vi.fn()
+myMockFn.mockThrow(new Error('error message'))
+myMockFn() // throws Error<'error message'>
+```
+
+## mockThrowOnce <Version>4.1.0</Version> {#mockthrowonce}
+
+```ts
+function mockThrowOnce(value: unknown): Mock<T>
+```
+
+Accepts a value that will be thrown during the next function call. If chained, every consecutive call will throw the specified value.
+
+```ts
+const myMockFn = vi
+  .fn()
+  .mockReturnValue('default')
+  .mockThrowOnce(new Error('first call error'))
+  .mockThrowOnce('second call error')
+
+expect(() => myMockFn()).toThrow('first call error')
+expect(() => myMockFn()).toThrow('second call error')
+expect(myMockFn()).toEqual('default')
+```
+
